conservation.condition_narrative: "Sprayed with butyl methacrylate polymer, March 1945, by Keck" (Keck typed label). "Cleaned and sprayed September, 1963, by Fine Arts Conservation Laboratories -- with co-polymer iso and n-butyl methacrylate" (typed).
conservation.report_notes: Published with corresponding artwork entry in *Georgia O’Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné* (Lynes, 1999), this historical conservation information documents treatment decisions made during the artist’s lifetime. Lynes quotes information found on backing labels, and, when noted, from other sources.

cr-1999: Backing: 1. OK {5star} (graphite) 2. "New York . . . / by Geo." [backing is torn] (AS, black crayon) 3. "New York – East River / 1928 / Georgia O'Keeffe" (WE, AAP6, black ink) 4. AAP11 [twice] 5. "Box 37" (DB, black ink) (Source: Lynes, 1999)

other.content: Initialed (verso, in center of five-pointed star, in graphite): OK (Source: The Met, 2025)

cr_data.provenance: The artist; [Doris Bry, New York]; Sidney and George Perutz, Dallas (in 1969); [Doris Bry, New York; until 1971; sold in 1971 to the artist]; the artist (1971–d. 1986; her bequest as part of the Alfred Stieglitz Collection to MMA) (Source: The Met, 2025)

description: The East River, wide and bluish-gray in color, runs between its two banks, which are covered with buildings. On both banks, the bright white roofs of multistory buildings are visible. Tall, thin smokestacks send white puffs into the air.
title: River, New York
